name: Workday

composio.note: Composio has no managed Workday app. You bring OAuth2 credentials, and those come from each customer's tenant. Expect one auth config per customer.

verdict.headline: You can't register a Workday OAuth app yourself; each customer's Workday admin must register your client in their own tenant.
verdict.summary: There is no public developer console or self-serve sandbox. OAuth clients live inside a customer's tenant, created by their security admin with chosen functional-area scopes. The hard part is tenant access: you need a design-partner customer or a formal Workday partnership. Once you have a tenant, the technical setup takes about an hour.

toProduction.label: 1–3 months for the first customer; 1–6 weeks per extra customer

activeEffort.label: 4–12 hours (yours) plus 1–2 hours of customer-admin time

approval.name: Customer's internal security review (and Workday partner certification only if you want a Marketplace listing)
approval.trigger: Every customer tenant. Workday itself does not review a plain API client; the customer's admin decides.
approval.wait: Days to weeks per customer; unknown for partner programs.

prerequisites.text: Access to a Workday tenant (customer sandbox/implementation tenant or partner tenant). Not self-serve.
A customer admin with the Security Administration domain (System functional area) to run Register API Client.
For integration clients: Integration Security domain access as well.
A list of the functional areas (scopes) and domain permissions your agent needs.
A Composio project and the Workday OAuth2 redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

oauth.refreshTokens: Admin chooses per client. 'Non-Expiring Refresh Tokens' makes them never expire (documented). Without it, a timeout applies; third-party snippets cite 1–365 days with a 30-day default (not confirmed on a fetched Workday page). ISU refresh tokens are generated by the admin via Manage Refresh Tokens for Integrations.
oauth.redirectUriRules: Set per client in the Redirection URI field; must match exactly what Composio sends. Third-party snippets say HTTPS only and comma-separated for multiple URIs (not confirmed on a fetched Workday page).

steps.title: Find a design-partner customer (or a partner tenant)
steps.detail:
Workday has no self-serve developer signup. You need access to a real Workday tenant. Realistic paths:
- A customer who agrees to be a design partner and gives you access to their **sandbox or implementation tenant**.
- A formal Workday partner program (Innovation Partner / Built on Workday). Workday's public pages describe these programs but do not state sandbox terms, fees, or eligibility for small vendors.

steps.title: Agree scope and security with the customer's Workday team
steps.detail: Send the customer a short spec: which functional areas (scopes) you need, read vs write, whether actions run as each user (Authorization Code) or as a service account (Integration System User), and your exact redirect URI. Security review on their side is the usual wait. Timing is our estimate, not documented.

steps.title: Customer admin registers the API client
steps.detail:
In their tenant, the admin searches for the **Register API Client** task and sets:
- Client Name
- Client Grant Type: `Authorization Code Grant`
- Access Token Type: `Bearer`
- Redirection URI: the URI from your Composio auth config
- Support PKCE: optional
- Non-Expiring Refresh Tokens: usually enabled
- Scope (Functional Areas): only what you need

Workday then shows the Client ID and Client Secret. Copy the secret right away.

steps.title: (Service-account path) Create an ISU and security group
steps.detail:
If your agent acts as a system, not as each user, the admin instead:
- Runs **Create Integration System User** (no UI sessions, exempt from password expiry).
- Creates an Integration System Security Group, adds the ISU, grants domain permissions.
- Runs **Activate Pending Security Policy Changes**.
- Uses **Register API Client for Integrations** with Non-Expiring Refresh Tokens, then **Manage Refresh Tokens for Integrations** to generate a refresh token for the ISU.

Composio's Workday toolkit is OAuth2 (user consent flow), so this path may not fit it directly.

steps.title: Customer admin sends you the endpoints and credentials
steps.detail: Ask for the values on the **View API Clients** page: Authorization Endpoint, Token Endpoint, REST API endpoint, plus Client ID and Secret. Hosts differ per data center and the auth host can differ from the token host. Agree on a secure channel for the secret.

steps.title: Create the auth config in Composio
steps.detail:
Composio dashboard: **Create Auth Config → Workday → OAuth2**, paste client ID and secret. Or create it by API (`composio.auth_configs.create` with `use_custom_auth`, `auth_scheme: OAUTH2`, `credentials: {client_id, client_secret, oauth_redirect_uri}`).

Redirect URI: Composio documents `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback` and says some toolkits still default to the legacy `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`. Use the value the dashboard shows for Workday; it is authoritative. The customer must register that exact URI.

Because each customer has its own client, plan **one auth config per customer tenant**.

steps.title: Connect a test user and make one API call
steps.detail: A Workday user in the customer tenant (with the right security groups) completes consent. Call a low-risk read endpoint (e.g. a worker lookup). Expect 403s until the user's or ISU's domain permissions cover the data.

steps.title: Verify long-lived refresh
steps.detail: Leave the connection idle past one access-token lifetime and confirm refresh works. If the client was not set to non-expiring refresh tokens, connections will die after the refresh timeout.

steps.title: Customer moves the client to production tenant
steps.detail: API clients do not carry over from sandbox to production on their own (our understanding; sandbox tenants are refreshed from production). The admin repeats registration in production, often after a change-control review. You get a new client ID/secret and endpoints, so a new auth config.

steps.title: Repeat per new customer
steps.detail: Every new customer runs the same registration in their tenant. Ship a one-page setup guide (fields, scopes, redirect URI, ISU steps) so their admin can do it without a call. Automate auth-config creation per customer with Composio's API.

scopes.name: Tenant Non-Configurable
scopes.purpose: Base access many APIs depend on; integration guides say always include it

scopes.name: Integration
scopes.purpose: Integration-level operations; listed by several vendors

gotchas.title: No self-serve tenant
gotchas.detail: You cannot sign up for a Workday developer tenant. Without a customer or a partner agreement, you have nowhere to register a client or test. Start the design-partner conversation first.

gotchas.title: Scopes are not enough; domain security decides
gotchas.detail: Functional-area scopes on the client only open the door. The user or ISU also needs domain permissions in a security group, and the admin must run **Activate Pending Security Policy Changes**. Missing either shows up as empty results or 403s.

gotchas.title: Refresh tokens expire unless the admin opts out
gotchas.detail: If Non-Expiring Refresh Tokens is off, connections die after the refresh timeout (commonly 30 days). One report shows a token failing with 401 after ~10 hours with the option off. Ask the admin to enable it.

gotchas.title: Hosts differ per tenant and per endpoint
gotchas.detail: The authorize host (e.g. `impl.workday.com`) and the token/API host (e.g. `wd2-impl-services1.workday.com`) can differ. Copy both from View API Clients; don't guess from the login URL.

gotchas.title: Secret is shown once
gotchas.detail: Workday shows the Client Secret only at registration. If the admin loses it, they must regenerate it.

gotchas.title: One auth config per customer
gotchas.detail: Each tenant issues its own client ID/secret and endpoints, so a single shared Composio auth config won't work across customers. Create configs by API.

gotchas.title: ISU passwords expire by default
gotchas.detail: If you use an ISU, the admin should exempt it from password expiry, which otherwise hits after three months.

blockers.symptom: Redirect or 'invalid redirect_uri' error at the Workday consent page
blockers.fix: Customer admin edits the API client and sets Redirection URI to the exact URI from your Composio auth config.

blockers.symptom: Token call works but API returns 403 or empty data
blockers.fix: Add the needed domain permissions to the user's or ISU's security group and run Activate Pending Security Policy Changes. Check the client has the matching functional area.

blockers.symptom: Connection works, then fails weeks later with 'refresh token expired' / 401
blockers.fix: Ask the admin to enable Non-Expiring Refresh Tokens on the client, then reconnect.

blockers.symptom: Customer's IT says 'we don't register third-party clients without review'
blockers.fix: Send a security packet: scopes and why, data stored, user vs ISU model, redirect URI, revocation steps. Expect weeks.
Find a design-partner customer with a sandbox, or apply to a Workday partner program via the partner portal.

unknowns: Endpoint probes were not run: authorize/token URLs are tenant-specific and no tenant host was available.
The authorize URL pattern comes from third-party docs; Workday's own reference for it is behind Workday Community login.
Refresh token timeout range (1–365 days, default 30) and HTTPS-only redirect rule come from search snippets of Workday Adaptive Planning docs we could not open.
Whether Non-Expiring Refresh Tokens is on by default (sources disagree).
Access token lifetime (not found in public docs).
Eligibility, cost and sandbox terms of Workday partner programs for small vendors.
Whether Composio's Workday toolkit asks for tenant/host fields at connect time, and the exact redirect URI it shows.
Whether API clients survive a sandbox refresh from production.

objects.name: Workers
objects.description: Employees and contingent workers: names, positions, managers, contact data
objects.note: Scopes alone return nothing. The user or ISU also needs Worker Data domain permissions (e.g. Worker Data: Public Worker Reports, Worker Data: All Positions), granted by the customer admin. Treat as PII.

objects.name: Organizations
objects.description: Supervisory orgs, cost centers, companies, locations
objects.note: Needs domain permissions such as Manage: Organization Integration and Manage: Location on the integration security group.

objects.name: Job profiles and positions
objects.description: Job profiles, job families, positions and their status
objects.note: Available as REST resources in integration tools. Which domain policy covers them varies by tenant; ask the admin.

objects.name: Time off
objects.description: Time off entries and balances per worker
scopes: Time Off and Leave (functional area name may differ)
objects.note: Integration tools expose worker time off entries. The exact functional area and domain policy names are behind Workday Community login and were not confirmed.

objects.name: Compensation and payslips
scopes: Compensation / Payroll (functional area name may differ)
objects.note: Highly sensitive. Most tenants limit compensation domains to a few security groups, so expect the admin to refuse or scope it narrowly. Do not request it unless the agent needs it.

objects.name: Recruiting
objects.description: Job requisitions, postings, candidates, job applications
objects.note: Needs domains such as Job Requisition Data, Job Postings: External and Candidate Data: Job Application. Candidate data is PII.

changes.detail: Workday has no general webhook API a developer can register. Push is possible only if the customer admin sets up an outbound subscription or notification on business process events, sent to a public endpoint you host (often SOAP-style messages). Otherwise poll: REST and SOAP (Workday Web Services) with updated/effective-date filters, or RaaS custom reports with date prompts and a stored watermark. Effective-dated records can appear more than once, so dedupe. Workday is bring-your-own auth on Composio, so polling triggers are not held to the 15-minute minimum that applies to Composio-managed apps.

limits.text: Workday publishes no fixed per-second rate limit. Under load it rejects requests: HTTP 429 for REST and RaaS, HTTP 500 for SOAP and RaaS. Retry with exponential back-off.
RaaS extract requests are capped by customer size, e.g. 75,000 per 24 hours and 15,000 per 60 minutes for tenants under 3,500 workers.
Web service responses max out at 1 million instances. Paged result caches last 2 hours between pages and 30 minutes after the last page.
Limits are per tenant and shared with the customer's other integrations, so your sync competes with theirs.
Composio-managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can poll faster. Workday has no managed app, so your own interval applies.

restrictions.text: Workday may throttle or suspend an integration or web service at its discretion when limits are exceeded.
Worker, candidate and compensation data is employee PII. Expect each customer to require a data processing agreement and security review before granting access, and to limit storage and retention.
Workday's API terms and data-use rules for partners sit behind Workday Community or partner agreements; we could not read them. Do not assume you may use the data for model training.
